title: Which Parable Describes Your Life Right Now?
subtitle: Jesus told stories. Which one is yours this week?

questions.text: What's the loudest feeling in your week?

options.text: I'm walking home after running too long.
Someone needs help and I keep seeing them.
I keep wondering if any of this is taking root.
Something small in me is growing.

questions.text: What does God's love feel like to you right now?

options.text: Like a Father running toward me.
Like a shepherd carrying me on His shoulders.
Like a Lord saying 'well done' over my small obedience.
Like a mercy I don't deserve but keep receiving.

questions.text: Pick the prayer you've prayed most this month:

options.text: Father, I have sinned. Let me come home.
God be merciful to me a sinner.
Lord, give me eyes to see the person in front of me.
Make this small thing You gave me bear fruit.
Soil that finally feels ready.
Something tiny that hasn't bloomed yet.
Steward season, using what I've been given.
Found season. He came after me.

questions.text: How do you handle other people's mess?

options.text: Cross the road to help them.
Leave the ninety-nine to go after the one.
Throw a party when they come home.
Catch myself judging, then ask for mercy.

questions.text: Pick the line that hits hardest right now:

options.text: He had compassion, and ran.
Well done, thou good and faithful servant.
God be merciful to me a sinner.
He layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
From a tiny seed of faith I almost dismissed.
From hearing the word and finally letting it settle.
From doing the next faithful thing with what I have.
From compassion that's spilling into action.

questions.text: If Jesus told a story about you this week, the moral would be...

options.text: The Father always runs.
Compassion crosses roads.
Small obediences matter.
Mercy is bigger than my mess.

prodigal-son.name: The Prodigal Coming Home
prodigal-son.description: You're walking home after a long time away, and the Father is already running. You don't need a polished speech. You just need the nerve to keep walking toward His arms.

good-samaritan.name: The Good Samaritan
good-samaritan.description: You see the person everyone else walked past. Your love isn't theoretical. It bandages wounds and pays the bill and comes back the next day to check in. That's the kingdom in real time.

sower.name: The Sower's Good Soil
sower.description: The Word is finally landing on ground that's been broken open. Don't let the slow pace scare you. Your fruit is coming, and it's coming in thirties and sixties and hundreds.

mustard-seed.name: The Mustard Seed
mustard-seed.description: Right now your faith feels tiny, almost embarrassingly so. But this is the season where God grows whole trees from things you can barely see.

lost-sheep.name: The Lost Sheep Carried Home
lost-sheep.description: You don't have to find your way back. He came after you. He's carrying you on His shoulders and rejoicing the whole way home. Let Him.

talents.name: The Faithful Steward
talents.description: You're using what God put in your hand instead of burying it out of fear. The reward isn't more stuff. It's more of Him saying 'well done.'

pharisee-and-tax-collector.name: The Tax Collector at the Back
pharisee-and-tax-collector.description: You won't even lift your eyes, and that's the exact posture God justifies. The simplest prayer in scripture is the one you've been praying: God, be merciful to me.
